outcome: Serum vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF-A) levels
Serum vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 (VEGFR-1) levels
Serum vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR-2) levels
Serum free placental growth factor (fPGF) levels
cohort: The study included 88 pregnant women, consisting of 32 with mild preeclampsia, 32 with severe preeclampsia, and 24 healthy normotensive controls.
finding: Serum levels of endostatin, VEGFR-1, and VEGF-A were significantly increased in preeclamptic women, while PAPP-A, VEGFR-2, and fPGF were significantly lower in preeclamptic women compared to healthy pregnant women, but these factors did not significantly distinguish between mild and severe preeclampsia.
cross-section timing: During pregnancy, at the time of diagnosis of preeclampsia.
birth_weight: Significantly lower in women with mild and severe preeclampsia compared to the control group.
gest_age: Significantly lower at birth in women with mild and severe preeclampsia compared to the control group.
